principles.text: Buying inside the range (not after breakout) is preferred because the stock isn't extended and the range gives the tightest stop; you don't need to wait for it to go higher.
You never know if a breakout will hold or fail and you don't need certainty; focus only on managing downside risk and finding the tightest entry.

In a fast V-shaped/lockout-rally market where many leaders break out the same day, strict progressive exposure can hold you back; be more aggressive. Progressive exposure fits long bases, not V-shaped bounces off a low.

Conviction to get aggressive comes from both the number of strong-looking individual stocks and the strong recovery of the indices/IWM, which are correlated since stocks make up the index; healthy breadth (not just Mag-7) matters.
Don't blindly follow any concept learned from other traders (including his own advice); test it against whether the market actually rewards you trading that way.
The market doesn't care about your P&L or equity curve; whether you're up 10% or down 10% is irrelevant to the trades, which reduces emotional pressure.
Panic-selling a clean breakout for fear it will fail is a mistake; forget it and move on, there will be many more opportunities.
